To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of diandric diploid triploids at conception is 0.2-0.3%, the frequency of dispermic triploids at the time of conception is 0-1%, and the frequency of diploid triploidy at the time of abortion is 0.5-0.6%.
the frequencies of diploidy in spermatozoa from oligozoospermics are higher than in sperm from normozoospermics, and that diploid sperm are more likely to be found in infertile than in fertile men.
(a) most diandric diploid triploids are the result of dispermy, and (b) the percentage of diploid sperm increases in infertile men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the frequency of diploid and haploid sperm and its relationship to the origin of triploid zygotes.
the origin of triploidies and with the origin of aneuploidies in spontaneous abortions.
the origin and incidence of diploid sperm and the role of these gametes in human reproduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diploid sperm are not a major cause of diandric, diploid triploidy in the general population, while they could be a major factor in the origin of this aneuploidy in oligozoospermia.
the frequencies of diandry at conception are good estimators of the frequencies of diploidy in the male germ cells.

the frequencies of diploidy in spermatozoa are similar to those of diandric diploid zygotes in the general male population, and are in the same order of magnitude as the frequencies of diandrics in spontaneous abortions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of diploid, dispermy sperm in normozoospermia is 0.5% (range, 0.2-0.9%).
the estimated frequency of sperm diploidy in infertile men is in good correlation with frequencies of diandry at conception, and with the frequency of diploid male pronuclei in ICSI zygotes.
1.2-2% of sperm in the ejaculate of normozoospermia men are diploid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
triploidy is a frequent chromosome abnormality in early spontaneous abortions.

the frequencies of diploids in sperm from infertile males, estimated from the frequencies of triploidy at fertilization, are in good correlation with those obtained directly from the study of sperm and zygotes.
the origin of diploid sperm can be studied using triploidy in spontaneous abortions and 3PN zygotes produced by ICSI.
